paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: one generation's faith doesn't automatically become the next generation's faith. The people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and the elders who had seen all His great works (Judges 2:7). Then another generation rose up who "did not know the LORD or the works that He had done for Israel" (Judges 2:10). Same LORD, same land, and a whole new crowd who didn't know Him.

And look at the pattern the LORD shows us. Israel turned away, trouble came, the people groaned, and the LORD raised up judges to save them, because He "was moved to pity by their groaning" (Judges 2:16, 18). But when the judge died, they became "even more corrupt than their fathers" (Judges 2:19). I think that's the hard part to sit with. Being rescued and being changed are two different things, and the LORD's mercy kept showing up anyway.

So what do I want you to take to your own counter? Don't count on yesterday's faith to carry you today. The nations the LORD left in the land were there to test whether Israel would keep His commandments (Judges 3:4), and Israel ended up living right in the middle of them, marrying into them and serving their gods (Judges 3:5-6). Stay in the Word, friend. Know the LORD for yourself, and tell somebody else what He has done. This story isn't over, either.
